Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal Shri Subodh Tamrakar, learned counsel for the appellant instead of pressing I.A. No.5709/2025, which is first application under Section 430(1) of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant Udaybhan Keer,
prays that this appeal be heard finally.
2. Accordingly, I.A. No.5709/2025 is dismissed as not pressed and with the consent of the parties,
this appeal is heard finally.

3. This criminal appeal under Section 374(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is filed by the convicted appellant - Udaybhan Keer being aggrieved of the judgment dated 05.09.2023 passed by the learned Second Additional District Judge, Gadarwara, District Narsinghpur (M.P.) in S.C.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21409 2 CRA-12803-2023 No. 19/2020, whereby the appellant has been convicted for offence under Section 366 of IPC and has been sentenced to to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 05 years and fine of Rs.2,000/- with default stipulation of additional R.I. for one month, under Section 376(3) of IPC and has been sentenced to to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 20 years and fine of Rs.5,000/- with default stipulation of additional R.I.
for three months and under Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act and has been sentenced to to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 20 years and fine of Rs.5,000/- with default stipulation of additional R.I.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that prosecutrix is major, she is a consenting party and appellant has been wrongly convicted.
5. Reading from evidence of PW-5, father of the prosecutrix, it is pointed out that in paragraphs No.11 and 12, has admitted that he has eight children, prosecutrix is youngest, sister just elder to the prosecutrix is aged about 24 year.

sentences.text: He has also admitted that prosecutrix is two years younger to the seventh child, whose age is reported to be 24 years.
Thus, age of the prosecutrix will comes out to about 22 years.

6. School Teacher, PW-7, has admitted, in paragraph 3 of his cross- examination, that Ex.P-11 is the date of birth scholar register in which date of birth is mentioned as 10.01.2005 and he cannot say as to on what basis said date of birth is recorded.
No documentary evidence is available with the school authorities to record the date of birth.

He has also admitted that he cannot say as to on what basis name of the father of prosecutrix was corrected in the register, Ex.P-11, and this correction was made on which day NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21409 3 CRA-12803-2023 and date and at the instance of which person.

He further admits that if the correction of name of the father of the prosecutrix carried out by him, there is neither any signature nor date or seal of the concerned school marked in the register.
7.
Dr. Babita Singh, PW-8, stated that secondary sexual characters of the prosecutrix were well developed.
There were no internal or external injury marks.
The hymen was old ruptured.
8. Prosecutrix (PW-3), in para 11, admitted that age of her elder sister is 24 years, they are eight brother and sisters.
She does not know the age of all the eight brother and sisters.
It is evident that there are contradictions in the statement of the prosecutrix.

In her court statement, prosecutrix stated that she had gone with the appellant as appellant had informed her that her father was not keeping good health but instead of taking her to her father's house, he had taken her to Bareli where he violated privacy.
In her 161 statements, Ex.D-3, she has stated that on 23.08.2020, she had gone to the house of her elder sister and Jhikoli Police Station, Saikheda where her third number sister had also come.
She had left her home because her father was talking about her marriage and that annoyed her, therefore, she left her home and had gone through Sagunghat (Barmaan).
Since, it was heavily raining and there was no phone with her sister, therefore, she could not informed her parents about her whereabouts.
On 04.09.2020, she had returned back to her father's house along with her father she has stated that nobody had taken her and no incident took place with her.
When she was confronted with statement Ex.D- 3 though she denied it but Ex.D-3 reveals her consent.
Age of the prosecutrix NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21409 4 CRA-12803-2023 could not be proved by the prosecution.
As per the evidence of the School Teacher, PW-7, and evidence of lady Doctor, PW-8, so also evidence of her father, PW-5, she appears to be major.
Prosecution has failed to discharge its burden that prosecutrix was minor at the time of the incident.
